name: Telegram AI bot with LangChain nodes
description: Uses LangChain nodes for advanced AI conversations and tool use in Telegram.

source.path: Telegram/Telegram AI bot with LangChain nodes.json

setup: "Execute Workflow Trigger" (executeWorkflowTrigger) started the original; run this workflow on demand, through the workflow API, or add a schedule.
"Listen for incoming events" (telegramTrigger) started the original; run this workflow on demand, through the workflow API, or add a schedule.
Workflow secret OPENAI_API_KEY: OpenAI API key for api.openai.com (Authorization: Bearer <secret>). Add it in the workflow editor's Secrets panel after import; never paste it in chat.
Provide run inputs: event, sessionId, chat_id, message, query.

hints: The original was a sub-workflow called by another workflow; pass its inputs as run inputs.
The original started from telegramTrigger; Yantra has no webhook slug for it, so run on demand, on a schedule (add a NodeCron), or via the workflow API with the event under the run input `event`.
"Generate image in Dall-E 3" authenticated with openAiApi in the original; add the matching Authorization header (or use the service's connector).
"AI Agent" kept conversation memory (memoryBufferWindow); sessionId is set to the run-input sessionId.
"AI Agent" used agent tools in the original: Dall-E 3 Tool (toolWorkflow). The cdecli agent calls connectors directly; connect credentials for the services those tools reached.
Select the Project and Environment on the Workflow Configs node (the ids from `cdecli auth status`), then connect a credential for each connector below.
Connect telegram: `cdecli credential create -n "telegram" -p telegram --template <formId> --secret <key>=<value>` (see `cdecli credential templates`).

notes: ## Generate an image with Dall-E 3 and send it via Telegram
